.claude/docs/commands.md: - Fonts missing in headless tests → `system-fonts` feature / fontconfig installed; stand checks need neither — they boot with the bundled DejaVu Sans alone, system fonts off, every generic family and any unavailable named family laying out in it by fallback (`seven_guis::stand::options`; checked by `stand_bundled_font_families`)

.claude/rules/security.md: - 2026-10-15: A listener or env read that only a test makes — served by no binary, reached by no caller — is no crossing and not the founder's call, yet it is registered as test-only in arch §Occupied Resources and the security plan's environment values before it lands, as `PAINT_TREE_BENCH_HTML` and `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` are (the operator's answer, 2026-10-15).

.claude/rules/testing.md: - 2026-11-23: While an editor's cargo (rust-analyzer's `cargo check --workspace`) runs on the shared `target/`, cargo can read a crate `Fresh` against sources just edited, so a test reads the pre-edit code — a re-run or a `touch` does not clear it and `cargo clean -p {crate}` does; a red that holds after an edit is first re-read after that clean, never taken as the edit's verdict.
.claude/rules/verification-harness.md: - 2026-10-31: State what a CI job did from that job's own log on both runs — a step's `completed · skipped` or `success`, the runner image and agent versions, a `df` line — never from the workflow YAML or one failing run: an `if:` can name no row that runs, and two jobs of one run can stand on different images.

.claude/rules/observability.md: - 2026-10-06: With the workspace's tracing 0.1.44, `tracing::error!(target: "…", a.b = x, "msg")` does not parse dotted field names (local macro ambiguity) and rejects string-literal keys — write `tracing::event!(target: "…", tracing::Level::ERROR, { a.b = x }, "msg")`.

.claude/rules/a11y.md: - 2026-10-06: On the dev host the AT-SPI bus reads `IsEnabled` false, so AccessKit's `update_if_active` never runs the tree build in a windowed boot — a windowed smoke proves the boot only; prove tree output headlessly through `Document::accessibility_tree`, and leave the bus flag alone (the operator's desktop state).
